answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed sediment-sampling season on one named glacier-fed river: the holder collects basalt-rich cores at fixed stations, each core's layered grains forming a fingerprint a hydrologist verifies in person. Random checks summon the holder to their own riverbank within a day, and one person cannot sample two rivers at once. The permit fee in outside money doubles per identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real river, another season of fieldwork, another human, and twice the prior fee.
